Vonoprazan and Carbonyl Iron: When used together, vonoprazan reduces the absorption of carbonyl iron in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to decreased levels or effects of carbonyl iron. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Clarithromycin and Cariprazine: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme involved in its metabolism. Dose reduction of cariprazine is required when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage adjustments. Close monitoring is essential. 3. Clarithromycin and Cefdinir: Clarithromycin reduces the effectiveness of cefdinir due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like clarithromycin may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like cefdinir. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Clarithromycin and Cefditoren: Similar to cefdinir, clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefditoren through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 5. Clarithromycin and Cefoxitin: Clarithromycin reduces the effects of cefoxitin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents may interfere with bactericidal agents. Monitor closely. 6. Clarithromycin and Cefpodoxime: Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefpodoxime due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Clarithromycin and Cefuroxime: Clarithromycin reduces the effects of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Close monitoring is advised. 8. Cenobamate and Clarithromycin: Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 9. Cenobamate and Vonoprazan: Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin and Ceritinib: Clarithromycin increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin and Cevimeline: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Clarithromycin and Chlordiazepoxide: Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Chloroquine and Clarithromycin: Chloroquine increases the toxicity of clarithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases chloroquine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Chlorpromazine and Clarithromycin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and Cholera Vaccine: Clarithromycin reduces the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid administering the vaccine to patients who have received systemic antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 16. Clarithromycin and Cholic Acid: Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Avoid inhibitors of the bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) to prevent liver toxicity. If co-administration is necessary, monitor liver function tests closely. 17. Clarithromycin and Ciclesonide (Inhaled): Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of inhaled ciclesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Vonoprazan and Cilostazol: Vonoprazan increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 19. Clarithromycin and Cilostazol: Clarithromycin increases cilostazol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Clarithromycin and Cimetidine: Clarithromycin increases cimetidine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, while cimetidine increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Clarithromycin and Cinacalcet: Clarithromycin increases cinacalcet levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Clarithromycin and Ciprofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Clarithromycin and Cisapride: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, significantly increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Vonoprazan and Citalopram: Vonoprazan increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Clarithromycin and Citalopram: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Clarithromycin and Cleviprex (Clevidipine): Clarithromycin increases clevidipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to hypotension, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Clarithromycin and Clofazimine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Clarithromycin and Clomipramine: Clarithromycin increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Clarithromycin and Clonazepam: Clarithromycin increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Vonoprazan and Clonidine: Vonoprazan increases clonidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Vonoprazan and Clopidogrel: Vonoprazan reduces clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Clarithromycin and Clopidogrel: Clarithromycin reduces clopidogrel activation by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Clarithromycin and Clorazepate: Clarithromycin increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Clarithromycin and Clozapine: Clarithromycin increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Clarithromycin and Cobicistat: Clarithromycin increases cobicistat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Clarithromycin and Colchicine: Clarithromycin increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 37. Clarithromycin and Conivaptan: Clarithromycin increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Clarithromycin and Conjugated Estrogens: Clarithromycin increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Clarithromycin and Copanlisib: Clarithromycin increases copanlisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin and Cortisone: Clarithromycin increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Clarithromycin and Crizotinib: Clarithromycin increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Clarithromycin and Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 in the gut. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Clarithromycin and Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 44. Clarithromycin and Cyclosporine: Clarithromycin increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Clarithromycin and Dabigatran: Clarithromycin increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Avoid co-administration in patients with renal impairment. 46. Clarithromycin and Dexamethasone: Clarithromycin increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Clarithromycin and Diazepam: Clarithromycin increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 48. Clarithromycin and Digoxin: Clarithromycin increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and altering intestinal flora. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Clarithromycin and Dihydroergotamine: Clarithromycin increases dihydroergotamine toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Clarithromycin and Diltiazem: Clarithromycin increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may lead to hypotension, bradycardia, and acute kidney injury. Use caution and monitor closely. This list provides a detailed explanation of drug interactions involving clarithromycin and other medications, emphasizing the mechanisms, clinical implications, and necessary precautions.
